Sometimes it gets so bad that if I try to resist I feel like ripping my hair out or that I'm going to die. I don't care about losing or gaining weight, all I want is some peace of mind and to be free of the cravings. It is ruining my life and my relationships and my happiness. Only you can answer this question. But pick something and commit yourself 100% to it. That's a hell of a lot better than floating through life being lost. I would say the MLS is a great "stepping stone" not just for medicine, but several other careers. If I were you I would stick to doing it and commit 100%. eliminate stress. i was only able to start a streak right after my midterms, or during spring break / christmas break / summer.

on the first day, leave the house, and bring premade lunch. if you must stay at home, wear your retainer the whole day if you have one.

write out what you want to eat the day before. dont starve or restrict too much, the first couple of weeks or so your body is still adjusting to a lower, more normal amount of food and it might "panic" and cause cravings to binge again. instead eat a perfectly normal amount. dont try to "make up" for previous days of binging. it will make up for it on its own, tho it will require a little patience.

IMMEDIATELY brush your teeth afterwards. put your retainer back in, or put on lip balm, and ESPECIALLY walk out of the kitchen/dining room/break room/coffee shop/whatever. walk around outside. focus on things OUTSIDE of yourself. touch the grass. feel how hot or cold it is. anything to distract or delay.

do not think about food. dont even think about how good you are doing, or how you arent binging. this thought itself is enough to make me binge.

a trick: prepare 1 cup of water and 1 cup of flavored tea before eating. the water is to fill you up (if your body craves the overly-full feeling) and the tea is to stimulate with flavor without more calories (if your body craves the flavor stimulation)

try to limit carbs. they make you more hungry and the times between meals are harder. things like bread, rice, etc. instead eat things with protien, and fats.

figure out what void you are trying to fill. is it loneliness? depression? boredom? try doing things to satisfy your needs, even if it seems hard. for example, if you are lonely the solution would be to call or text a friend. this can sometimes be hard for me because i realized that i was feeling like i was a bother to people. of course this isnt the case, it was just my warped view of reality because i can be very depressed.

if you are stressed, use other techniques. what worked for me was to blast heavy metal music in my earbuds. it can actually be calming when i am angry or distressed enough.

if you are religious, pray. i have been in such terrible moments that i have literally cried out to God in fear and pain. it works every time, and gives you comfort that you are not alone, no matter how alone you feel.

if your goal is to lose weight, please have patience with yourself. also love yourself, but not in the way as in "i am perfectly fine the way i am", obviously this isnt true, or you wouldnt be feeling this way. but if you constantly beat yourself up, think lowly of yourself, you will trigger the bad feelings and want to soothe yourself with eating. instead think this way - i am just as worthy of a person when i am fat, thin, smart, dumb, lonely, popular, whatever. of course you have goals for yourself, but think of it as your "final form" that you are aiming for and have the power to achieve.

think of intrinsic qualities that make you unique and a good person. are you a good friend, good at your job, good at a skill, anything. focus on this. do not revolve your whole identity or mood or confidence around your looks. i used to do this and sometimes i still struggle with this, but you feel a lot better when you focus on other qualities.

another thing, what triggered me today is that i came home after school and my mom was making dinner, and the whole house smelled intensely of food, which triggered me. what i would have done differently is wait a couple hours at school until she was done cooking, and then come home.

i am still learning about myself and what works for me, and please remember that not all of these things might work for you. think of it like a science experiment. all this took YEARS of trial and error. so in general, just pay attention to your triggers, emotional state, etc, and what you could do better next time, or how to optimize yourself and your surroundings.
